pages.text: Justice Outcomes Explorer (JOE) Justice Outcomes Explorer (JOE) Skip Navigation Justice Outcomes Explorer (JOE) May 01, 2024 The Justice Outcomes Explorer (JOE) is a Census Bureau experimental data product that measures the economic and health outcomes of people who have been involved with the criminal justice system. Criminal justice involvement can include criminal charges, prison releases, and probation and parole sentences. Outcomes measured include employment, earnings, government program participation, and mortality. JOE is a collaboration between the U.S. Census Bureau and the University of Michigan that uses Criminal Justice Administrative Records System (CJARS) data to better understand how people involved in the justice system reintegrate into society. JOE covers criminal justice system involvement at any point between 2000 and 2020. Actual coverage of justice involvement depends on the coverage of agencies in the CJARS data, while coverage of outcomes depends on the availability of source data at the Census Bureau. Data users can download JOE data below or interact directly with the JOE data using the data visualization tool hosted by the University of Michigan. The tool includes additional justice-related outcomes created from CJARS without Census Bureau data. Experimental data products are innovative statistical products created using new data sources or methodologies that benefit data users in the absence of other relevant products. Justin Bis Justin Bis is the Chief of Staff for the Office of Technology Commercialization (OTC) at the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE). In this role, he works alongside OTC leadership to maximize the impact of DOE’s investments in technology commercialization, strengthen coordination across the agency, and ensure long-term success. Mr. Bis has more than a decade of experience in government service and public life. He previously served at the White House as Special Assistant to President Trump and Deputy Director of the Presidential Personnel Office, where he managed the appointment of senior government officials responsible for regulating the U.S. financial and energy markets. At DOE, he was the Director of Intergovernmental and External Affairs under Secretary Dan Brouillette, serving as the department’s primary liaison to trade associations, labor unions, and state, local, and tribal governments. Beyond his federal service, Mr. Bis was the Executive Director of the Ohio Republican Party and Ohio Deputy State Director for the Donald J. Trump for President campaign. He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Northern Michigan University.

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn K2-Play Completes Final Phase of North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan Oct 15, 2026 FRUITA, Colo. – Over the past eight years, the North Fruita Desert has changed in ways riders can see as soon as they arrive. There are more miles of singletrack, more places to camp and dedicated space for races and other large events, all part of a broader effort by the Bureau of Land Management and community partners to keep pace with one of western Colorado’s busiest recreation areas. This fall, the final trail in the North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan is complete. K2-Play winds for about three miles along the base of the Book Cliffs and completes the final phase of a roughly 30-mile expansion of the 18 Road trail system. Its completion caps years of planning and construction involving the BLM Grand Junction Field Office, Colorado Plateau Mountain Bike Trail Association, Mesa County, City of Fruita, local businesses, professional trail builders and volunteers. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/si-redefinition/kilogram/kilogram-kibble-balance SI Redefinition Kilogram: The Kibble Balance Named after its inventor, Bryan Kibble at the U.K.’s National Physical Laboratory (NPL) , who conceptualized it in 1975, the Kibble balance is an exquisitely accurate weighing machine. Like any balance, it is designed to equalize one force with another: In this case, the weight of a test mass is exactly offset by a force produced when an electrical current is run through a coil of wire immersed in a surrounding magnetic field. The surrounding field is provided by a large permanent magnet system or an electromagnet. The moveable coil, once electrified, becomes an electromagnet with a field strength proportional to the amount of current it conducts. When the coil's field interacts with the surrounding magnetic field, an upward force is exerted on the coil. The magnitude of that force is controlled by adjusting the current. Basic principles of the Kibble balance, a device that can be used to measure mass. Credit: Suplee/NIST The instrument was originally called a "watt” balance because it makes measurements of both current and voltage in the coil, the product of which is expressed in watts, the SI unit of power. Kimberly Ballou Kimberly Ballou serves as Chief of Staff for the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of International Affairs (IA), a role she resumed in June 2026 after previously serving in the position during a period of leadership transition in early 2025. She has more than two decades of experience advancing U.S. international energy policy, global energy security, strategic partnerships, and international cooperation. Throughout her career, Kimberly has held senior leadership positions across IA, including Senior Advisor for Strategic Operations to the IA Assistant Secretary, Acting Director for Asian Affairs, Deputy Director for American Affairs, and Senior Advisor for Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean. Phil Westcott From Juneau, to Anchorage, to Nome, and beyond, people in Alaska are often spotted wearing a colorful or patterned hooded garment with a big front pocket. This classic Alaska attire is known as a kuspuk. Kuspuk is an English word based on the Indigenous Yup’ik word “qaspeq” which translates to “cloth over parka.” The original qaspeq was made from gut skin, animal hide, or feathered bird skin to keep the wearer warm and dry—a constant struggle known all too well by those who have live, work, and travel in the arctic. In the 1800s, European whalers brought goods to trade, which included cloth bags filled with flour or sugar. Indigenous (Inupiaq/Yup’ik) women repurposed the cotton flour sacks and sewed a lightweight summer garment that resembled the “over parkas” worn in the winter.Today, kuspuks are often made of colorful or patterned cotton material and are locally hand-made. La higiene y prevención de virus respiratorios 18 de ago. del 2025 English (US) Lo que debe saber La higiene es un hábito o una práctica regular que mejora la limpieza. Practicar una buena higiene es una estrategia de prevención principal recomendada para todos para disminuir los riesgos de presentar enfermedades respiratorias. Recomendación Practique una buena higiene al cubrirse la nariz y la boca al toser y estornudar, lavarse o desinfectarse las manos con frecuencia, y limpiar las superficies que se tocan frecuentemente. Cómo funciona Cubrirse la nariz y la boca al toser y estornudar limita la propagación de microbios para proteger a los demás. Lavarse las manos con jabón elimina los microbios de las manos, lo que hace que sea menos probable que infecten el sistema respiratorio cuando se toca los ojos, la nariz o la boca. Si no hay agua y jabón disponibles, usar un desinfectante de manos con al menos un 60 por ciento de alcohol puede matar estos microbios. Lab-Embedded Entrepreneurship Program (OTC) What is LEEP? The U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Office of Technology Commercialization (OTC) Lab-Embedded Entrepreneurship Program (LEEP) recruits the best and brightest through a national call for a two-year funded fellowship. This fellowship provides innovators who have early-stage energy startups and/or emerging technologies with the support needed to develop and transition their ideas into the market. These entrepreneurs are embedded for a period of two years at one of four national labs where they are mentored by a lab scientist. LEEP also provides support at the local, regional, and national levels including entrepreneurship training and a networking ecosystem to address the hurdles traditionally faced by early-stage energy and manufacturing technology startups. What are the impacts of LEEP? The U.S. makes major investments in basic and applied energy and manufacturing research, at both universities and DOE National Labs. Laboratory Testing for Diphtheria For Public Health July 31, 2026 Key points Clinical laboratories can use various methods to identify Corynebacterium diphtheriae , but identification alone isn't enough for diagnosis confirmation. CDC uses culture and molecular methods, and a specialized toxin production test to confirm diphtheria diagnoses. Confirmatory testing informs clinical management and public health action to prevent further spread. Stay informed on the latest diphtheria specimen acceptance criteria. Overview Laboratories must follow a series of steps in order to confirm a diphtheria diagnosis: Identifying and isolating C. diphtheriae Detecting the diphtheria toxin ( tox ) gene Showing diphtheria toxin production Confirmation of toxin production is key Toxin-producing strains of C. diphtheriae cause diphtheria. Most U.S. strains that possess the tox gene don't express it or produce toxin. Therefore, tests that identify C. diphtheriae or detect the tox gene but don't confirm toxin production are insufficient to confirm a diphtheria diagnosis. Real-time RT-PCR is the preferred method to confirm mumps; it's more sensitive and specific than serologic assays to detect IgM. Railroads carried the coal from Scranton to the cities of the Northeast and in barges across the Great Lakes to the Midwest provide fuel to heat the nation. By the late 1880s, Scranton had become one of the nation’s leading industrial centers. Coal mining, railroading, iron works, and textile manufacturing were prevalent, and the Lackawanna Valley’s economic promise attracted laborers and capitalists from across the country, and the world. The northern extremities of the Black Rock Desert lie to the east and west. Elevations range from 6,120 feet to 8,799 feet. The Natural Area was established in 1973 to ensure the preservation of the Lahontan Cutthroat Trout, a threatened species of fish, in its natural habitat and to maximize available spawning areas. Natural features of the area consists of scattered stands of aspen and mountain mahogany, mountains and creeks. To protect the threatened trout, fishing is prohibited. Clear, pristine streams make it possible to observe and photograph the fish. Using zero taxpayer dollars, the LWCF invests earnings from offshore oil and gas leasing to help strengthen communities, preserve our history and protect our national endowment of lands and waters. The LWCF program is divided into the " State Side " which provides grants to State and local governments, and the " Federal Side " which is used to acquire lands, waters, and interests therein necessary to achieve the natural, cultural, wildlife, and recreation management objectives of federal land management agencies. Any claim for refund or credit may be reviewed by the IRS. If you claim a refund or credit on your federal tax return of more than $2 million ($5 million for a C corporation), the IRS must review the refund or credit and provide a report to the Joint Committee on Taxation (JCT). Refunds or credits for which a report must be provided to the JCT are referred to here as a Joint Committee refund case (“JC refund case”). The JCT is a non-partisan committee of the United States Congress. pages.text: Largest 'Sea Dragon' Fossil Accidentally Discovered in Museum | National Geographic 1:00 Artist's impression of the Ichthyosaurus ILLUSTRATION BY JOSCHUA KNÜPPE Largest 'Sea Dragon' Fossil Accidentally Discovered in Museum The paleontologist who made the discovery was originally at the museum to study a fossil that resembles the Loch Ness monster. By Sarah Gibbens Published August 28, 2017 • 4 min read Sven Sachs, a paleontologist from the Bielefeld Natural History Museum in Germany, was at the Lower Saxony State Museum in Hannover to study an ancient sea reptile when one of the museum's display fossils caught his eye. The specimen had originally been unearthed in the mid-1990s in Somerset, England, but it had remained largely unstudied since. Sachs suspected it was an Ichthyosaurus. Commonly mistaken for a dinosaur, the species was more like a "sea dragon" marine reptile that had a long, flexible body and may have swum like eels. "I found it very extraordinary," said Sachs. "[It was] way bigger than any specimen I had examined." He explained the specimen had previously been labeled as a smaller species within the Ichthyosaurus group. Sachs reached out to Ichthyosaurus expert Dean Lomax from the University of Manchester, and in early 2017 they examined the specimen together, finding it to be a specimen of the species Ichthyosaurus somersetensis . Skeleton of Ichthyosaurus . Photograph by Dean Lomax Their findings, published in the journal Acta Palaeontologica Polonica , describe the largest known specimen of its kind. Prior to the SBA, he held numerous leadership positions with the US Army, including Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army for Diversity and Leadership. In 2005, he retired from the military as a Colonel and was appointed to the Senior Executive Service. They’re the ethereal patterns of light that coat the bottoms of swimming pools and break up the shadows of glass. Anywhere light is bent or reflected by a curved surface, caustics can appear. This trick of the light is turning out to be an important tool for 3D-printing metal, a process in which high-powered lasers melt metal powder one layer at a time. NIST scientists have found that caustic reflections from those lasers contain clues about the metal’s microscopic shape. pages.text: Lauren Boebert, once a MAGA star, loses her Colorado seat Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Lauren Boebert, once a MAGA star, loses her Colorado seat 5 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Sheila Flynn Senior US Reporter Getty Images Republican Lauren Boebert lost to a Democrat after three terms in Congress Lauren Boebert, the Republican representative from Colorado who rose to national fame as one of Donald Trump's biggest cheerleaders, has lost her seat in Congress. The race was too close to call on election night last week, but after every vote was counted the Democrat Eileen Laubacher has been declared the winner by the AP news agency. It means Boebert, who was one of the most vocal conservatives in the House of Representatives, will not serve a fourth term. The 39-year-old was one of the faces of Trump's "Make America Great Again" - or MAGA - movement, when she burst on to the Colorado political scene at the end of 2019. Like the president, she was not a career politician. Boebert first made headlines when she encouraged staff at her restaurant Shooters, located in a small Colorado town named Rifle, to openly carry firearms. Her rallies focused on gun rights and fighting - fighting Democrats, fighting the establishment, fighting illegal immigration or fighting anyone or anything that could be deemed "woke". Lauren Joyce Acting Chief Operating Officer Lauren Joyce serves as Acting Chief Operating Officer for the Office of Nuclear Energy (NE). She has over 17 years of federal government experience, including leadership roles within NE as Deputy Chief Operating Officer, Acting Chief of Staff, and Deputy Chief of Staff. Since joining the Department of Energy in 2008, Ms. Joyce has also completed a one-year detail to the White House - National Security Council as the Policy Advisor in the Directorate of European Affairs. Previously, she worked as a senior international relations specialist in DOE’s Office of American Affairs, focusing on energy, economic, and national security issues in Latin America and the Caribbean. Earlier in her career, Ms. Joyce served as a foreign affairs specialist in the Office of Nuclear Energy. Ms. Joyce holds a bachelor’s degree in English and History from Presbyterian College and an Executive Master’s in International Relations from the Maxwell School at Syracuse University.
